story: I got into tech when I was about 12. Back then, my first program was a batch script I'd send my friends over Skype to shut down their computers. It was simple, but I had fun with it.

Years later, I worked in IT infrastructure at a hospital. Sometimes computers would come in with several things wrong, and I'd have to make do with whatever parts I had on hand. I even held a CPU cooler in place with zip ties once, haha. The best part was figuring out what had gone wrong and getting the machine running again, even if it meant improvising a little.
I've been working in back-end development for almost five years, mostly with .NET. Getting to the bottom of a problem and fixing it is still one of my favorite things about working in tech.

Writing and art came from a different place. I got interested in both because of the things I'd experienced and, more than anything, the people who left a mark on me. Making things became a way to express what stayed with me, and I want people who read or see my work to take a moment to reflect, too.
I'll keep experimenting and digging deeper into these fields and plenty of others, always open to learning. After all, things I'm sure of today might look completely different to me in the future.

home.introduction: Hi, I'm John, someone who enjoys making things and experimenting across different fields. This site is my lab: I share my projects here and write about the whole creative process.

disciplines.software: I build and maintain applications and tools end-to-end, from the database and API to the interface, focusing on security and scalability.
disciplines.stories: I write stories and build their worlds and characters, focusing on how the relationships between them change with everything they go through.
